content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposed a new method for efficient ViT. The task is very interesting and has wide applications in real world. Different from existing works, the authors proposed a new model by learning semantic tokens (cluster centers) to reduce the input token numbers. Extensive experiments proved the proposed method achieves high performance even with lower computation cost.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
- A new way to achieve efficient ViT.
- Good performances compared to competitive methods.


Weakness:
- It is unclear whether the high performance when applying STViT comes from a better backbone baseline. Since there are some small modification to the existing DeiT model (e.g., replacing the original patch embedding layer), the base model is already higher than the standard DeiT model that used in the compared works. So Table 3 is not fair.

- Following the above concern, why STViT-DeiT-T even has higher accuracy than the base DeiT model? It doesn't make sense if the accuracy actually increased.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Overall quality is good. But I have some clarity questions about this paper:
I did not understand the visualization figure (Fig. 3). The attention maps look messy so I did not get the sentence "The attention layer groups the semantic information according to the position of initial cluster centers".

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper introduces a sparsification technique of queries to improve the efficiency of vision transformers while maintaining similar accuracy.   The queries are reduced by a spatial pooling operation with depthwise convolution. Besides, the proposed method is a general block, which can be embedded into several transformer-based frameworks and applied to downstream tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
+ The paper is well-written and well-organized. The motivation and visualization are clear.
+ The experiments and ablation studies are comprehensive. The comparison counterparts in the experiment are appropriate.

- The baseline method in the experiments is not selected fairly. The spatial pooling operation adopts a depthwise convolution to reduce the number of queries. It makes sense, but it can improve the accuracy of the framework itself rather than reducing the computational cost alone. This technique is demonstrated effectiveness in many existing methods, such as CSwin and PVTv2.
- The global cluster centers, actually the position embedding, also have similar problems. It can also improve the accuracy of the baseline framework. The paper needs to provide a more fair comparison to demonstrate the efficiency clearly.
- "the semantic tokens can be forced to represent more local and distinguished features". Why can the semantic tokens represent local features? The key and value are still global.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The clarity is clear and the reproducibility is good. But the novelty is somewhat limited.
content.summary_of_the_review: The main issue of the paper is the unfair comparison, making the efficiency gains in experiments unconvincing.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces Semantic Token ViT (STViT) for efficient global and local vision recognition. The primary idea is to introduce extra learnable tokens (as semantic tokens) for aggregating the information among original spatial tokens. Besides, the authors propose a dumbbell unit for dense prediction tasks. Experiments validate that the introduced architecture can reduce the computational complexity while achieving comparable/slightly-better performance on image classification, object detection, and instance segmentation tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
### Pros:

- The technical elaboration of the proposed method is straightforward.
- STViT has been extended to the local Vision Transformers, unlike the previous token pruning methods, which are designed for the image classification tasks. Designing an efficient transformer-based backbone for both classification and dense prediction tasks is practical.
- Extensive experiments (including image/video classifications, object detection and semantic segmentation) have been provided. However, I still hold some concerns about the ablation studies and unfair experimental settings, which are shown in the cons part.

### Cons:
- **Unclear Presentation**

The presentation of the methodology part could be clearer. For example, the motivation for introducing the global initial center tokens needs to be better elaborated. Please specify the reasons for adding extra learnable tokens that are initialized from a global perspective. Are there any reasons for utilizing Gaussian distribution for initialization? Are there any other choices?

Besides, the detailed architecture of STViT-R-Swin is not clear. A corresponding table is highly recommended to detail the architectures.

For the implementation of STViT-Swin, the semantic tokens are generated in Stage 3 and not downsampled in Stage 4. Is there any reason behind this choice?

- **Unfair and insufficient comparison**

For DeiT, this paper replaces the original patch embedding layer containing a 16 × 16 convolutional layer with four lightweight 3 × 3 convolutional layers. Previous works have demonstrated the strategy will make the training process stable and thus result in better performance. Comparing STViT+Deit(3x3 convs) with other token pruning methods (DeiT with 16x16 conv) is not fair. Please report the performance comparisons with other methods under exactly identical architectures.

Please also provide the Semantic segmentation experiments (for example, on ADE20K) for further validation.

- **Visualization**

The visualization in this paper can not effectively illustrate the motivation. For example, the figure 3 is weird. Since the paper claims that the extra-introduced learnable tokens are semantic-related, a more intuitive visualization should be provided to prove that each semantic token is primarily correlated with a certain image region. Otherwise, the state of semantic tokens is over-claimed. From figure 3, I can not tell the explicit relations.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The motivation of this paper is clear. However, considering the unclear statement on the methodology, the quality of this paper should be further improved.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, the paper provides extensive experiments to verify its effectiveness. The motivation is clear. Considering that it’s the first work to introduce an efficient transformer backbone for downstream tasks, I will give my rating as `marginally above the acceptance threshold`. However, the paper still needs to be improved. Considering the unfair and insufficient comparisons, and the unclear visualization, I suggest the author give further responses to the weakness part. Otherwise, I may downgrade my rating.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The quadratic computational complexity of the number of tokens still limits the practical applications of ViTs. This paper proposes a novel semantic token ViTs for efficient global and local vision transformers, which reduce most FLOPS and achieve faster inference speed. In addition, the author also does video recognition experiments to verify the generalization of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
+ The motivation is clear. The quadratic computational complexity of the number of tokens is an important but not solved problem currently.
+ Experimental results are promising, which achieve better performance with faster speed.

Weaknesses:
+ Experiments are not enough. Semantic segmentation, object detection, and instance segmentation results are not promising. In addition, the author also lacks some recent comparisons.
+ The implementation is not novel. Actually, there are a lot of recent works which combine local and global transformers for architectural design.
+ Global center tokens are not clear. Actually, we could achieve such semantic tokens in a clustering manner, which should be much more effective than global initial center tokens.
+ The motivation for using clustering semantic tokens is not clearly clarified.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper seeks to tackle an essential problem in ViTs. However, the motivation for the proposed method, experimental results, and lack of comparisons make me lead to give reject.

content.title: STViT: Semantic Tokens for Efficient Global and Local Vision Transformers
content.abstract: The quadratic computational complexity to the number of tokens limits the practical applications of Vision Transformers (ViTs). Several works propose to prune redundant tokens to achieve efficient ViTs. However, these methods generally suffer from (i) dramatic accuracy drops, (ii) application difficulty in the local vision transformer, and (iii) non-general-purpose networks for downstream tasks. In this work, we propose a novel Semantic Token ViT (STViT), for efficient global and local vision transformers, which can also be revised to serve as backbone for downstream tasks. The semantic tokens represent cluster centers, and they are initialized by pooling image tokens in space and recovered by attention, which can adaptively represent global or local semantic information. Due to the cluster properties, a few semantic tokens can attain the same effect as vast image tokens, for both global and local vision transformers. For instance, only 16 semantic tokens on DeiT-(Tiny,Small,Base) can achieve the same accuracy with more than 100% inference speed improvement and nearly 60% FLOPs reduction; on Swin-(Tiny,Small,Base), we can employ 16 semantic tokens in each window to further speed it up by around 20% with slight accuracy increase. Besides great success in image classification, we also extend our method to video recognition. In addition, we design a STViT-R(ecover) network to restore the detailed spatial information based on the STViT, making it work for downstream tasks, which is powerless for previous token sparsification methods. Experiments demonstrate that our method can achieve competitive results compared to the original networks in object detection and instance segmentation, with over 30% FLOPs reduction for backbone.
